necessary resources to meet contract requirements.

All
deliverables under this contract shall not be marked proprietary or confidential or with any other markings limiting
the Government’s use, unless otherwise specified by the Government.

1.1.4. The Contractor shall ensure that any of the contractor’s owned, leased, or chartered aircraft used in the performance
of this contract comply with all applicable local and long‑distance aircraft and pilot requirements, including those
applicable to both prime contractors and subcontractors.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall ensure its owned, leased, or chartered aircraft comply with applicable aircraft and pilot requirements.

Aircraft used for NASA traveler transportation shall be
certificated, operated, and maintained in accordance with the requirements of 14 CFR:
a. Part 21—Certification Procedures for Products and Parts
b. Part 25—Airworthiness Standards: Transport Category Airplanes Part 29—Airworthiness Standards:

Aviation Organization (ICAO), Federal, and industry standards.

Requirements include the following:
a. A structured means of safety risk management decision making.

c. Increased confidence in risk controls through structured safety assurance processes.
d. An effective interface for knowledge sharing.
e. A safety promotion framework to support a sound safety culture.

rows.verbatim:
2.1.1. The Contractor shall provide medical travel services in response to a worldwide medical event for NASA’s Human
Spaceflight Mission Directorate (HSMD), Johnson Space Center (JSC), or other travelers identified by NASA
(referred to as ‘traveler(s)’ throughout) on a pre-paid basis regardless of traveler’s home location or country of
origin.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide medical travel services worldwide for NASA HSMD/JSC travelers on a pre-paid basis.

rows.verbatim:
2.1.2. The Contractor shall transport the injured or ill traveler to nearest appropriate medical facility that practices U.S.
standards of medical care.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall transport injured or ill travelers to the nearest appropriate medical facility meeting U.S. standards of care.

rows.verbatim:
a. In the event that the medical facility does not meet the U.S. standards of medical care, the Contractor shall
provide sufficient rationale to the NASA/JSC Chief Medical Officer and NASA Contracting Officer
Representative (COR) for using the proposed facility.
rows.normalized: If the medical facility does not meet U.S. standards of care, Contractor shall provide rationale to the NASA/JSC Chief Medical Officer and COR.

rows.verbatim:
2.1.3. The Contractor shall co-develop with NASA the notification process for timely communication, integration and
operational protocols with NASA physicians, and dissemination of confidential medical reports.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall co-develop with NASA a notification process for communication, integration/operational protocols, and dissemination of confidential medical reports.

rows.verbatim:
2.1.4. The Contractor shall obtain all necessary insurance information from the traveler, as required, and shall
coordinate the payment of personal medical expenses incurred by the traveler that are not arranged for or
provided directly by the Contractor.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall obtain necessary insurance information from the traveler and shall coordinate payment of personal medical expenses not arranged by the Contractor.

rows.verbatim:
Such coordination shall be conducted exclusively between the Contractor, the traveler, and the
traveler’s insurer, without any involvement from the Government.
rows.normalized: Coordination of personal medical expense payment shall be conducted exclusively between Contractor, traveler, and traveler's insurer.

rows.verbatim:
2.1.5. The Contractor shall provide group membership as specified in Section B Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Group
Membership.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide group membership as specified in Section B FFP Group Membership.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide an “Air Ambulance Medical Evacuation” (medevac) service in response to a worldwide medical emergency for NASA’s Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate (HSMD), Johnson Space Center (JSC), or other travelers identified by NASA (referred to as ‘traveler(s)’ throughout) on a pre-paid basis regardless of traveler’s home location or country of origin.
rows.normalized: Found by the coverage check and not by the reader: The Contractor shall provide an “Air Ambulance Medical Evacuation” (medevac) service in response to a worldwide medical emergency for NASA’s Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate (HSMD), Johnson Space Center (JSC), or...

rows.verbatim: The Contractor and the traveler will handle all subsequent GOP and pay as agent reimbursements directly between themselves.
rows.normalized: The Contractor (together with the traveler) will handle all subsequent Guarantee of Payment and pay-as-agent reimbursements directly between themselves.

rows.verbatim:
b. The Contractor shall provide transportation for three accompanying travelers specified by NASA on the same
transport as the injured/ill individual requiring a medevac.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide transportation for three accompanying travelers specified by NASA on the medevac transport.

rows.verbatim:
c. In the event that the same transport cannot accommodate all three accompanying travelers, at least one
accompanying traveler specified by NASA shall be accommodated on the same transport.
rows.normalized: If the transport cannot fit all three accompanying travelers, at least one specified traveler shall be accommodated on the same transport.

rows.verbatim:
d. The Contractor shall provide sufficient rationale to the NASA Contracting Officer Representative (COR) why
it cannot transport all accompanying travelers and provide alternate transportation for the remaining
accompanying travelers within 24 hours to the same location as the injured or ill traveler.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide rationale to the COR and provide alternate transportation for remaining accompanying travelers within 24 hours.

rows.verbatim:
2.2.2. The Contractor provided services shall meet the Commission on Accreditation Medical Transport Services
(CAMTS), National Accreditation Alliance of Medical Transport Applications (NAAMTA) Global, and European
Aero-Medical Institute (EURAMI) accreditation standards or equivalent for personnel and assets.
rows.normalized: Contractor-provided services shall meet CAMTS, NAAMTA Global, and EURAMI accreditation standards or equivalent.

rows.verbatim:
Active credentials must be maintained according to the standard renewal timelines dictated by the respective accrediting
body.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain active credentials per accrediting body renewal timelines.

rows.verbatim:
Any deviations must be reported to the JSC Chief Medical Officer and Contracting Officer Representative
(COR), and approved by NASA prior to implementation, unless otherwise specified by the Contracting Officer.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report any deviations to the JSC Chief Medical Officer and COR and obtain NASA approval before implementation, unless the Contracting Officer specifies otherwise.

rows.verbatim:
a. The decision to perform a medevac shall be made jointly (50/50) by NASA and the
Contractor, who will apply U.S. standards of medical care.
rows.normalized: The decision to perform a medevac shall be made jointly by NASA and the Contractor, applying U.S. standards of medical care.

rows.verbatim: This independent third party will be mutually agreed upon within 30 calendar days of contract award.

upon request by NASA.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide medevac using a Portable Medical Isolation Unit upon NASA's request.

rows.verbatim:
a. If a medical event occurs, all costs for evacuation and additional medical travel services shall be the
responsibility of the Contractor and no additional cost beyond the prepaid provided group membership as
specified in Section B Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Group Membership amount will be incurred by NASA or its
travelers.
rows.normalized: If a medical event occurs, Contractor is responsible for all evacuation and additional medical travel costs beyond the prepaid group membership amount.

rows.verbatim:
2.3.1. The Contractor shall conduct a program status meeting each contract year with NASA management and JSC’s
Chief Medical Officer, with the first meeting happening within 90 calendar days of the start of the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall conduct an annual program status meeting, first meeting within 90 calendar days of contract start.

rows.verbatim:
2.3.2. The Contractor shall participate in NASA Contingency Tabletop simulations of evacuation events to validate
communication and operations plans and decision-making procedures (estimate twice per year).
rows.normalized: Contractor shall participate in NASA Contingency Tabletop simulations (approx. twice yearly).

rows.verbatim:
2.3.3. The Contractor shall provide, within 60 calendar days of contract start and update annually for currency by Oct
1st, a Medical Facility Support Plan for each of the Russia and Kazakhstan medical facilities identified by NASA
which contains the following:
a. Points of Contact (primary, alternate, and emergency) and communication protocols, including
language/translation support and expected response times.
b. Medical Capabilities and Transport Capabilities, including bed‑to‑bed transport feasibility, equipment
availability, access to specialized care, and any seasonal or regional constraints that may affect operations.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide (within 60 days, updated annually by Oct 1) a Medical Facility Support Plan containing items a-h; items a-b shown here, continued on next page (8 items total).

rows.verbatim:
c. Admittance, Use, GOP, and Discharge Processes, including procedures required to initiate care, provide
ongoing coordination, and transfer patients between facilities and medevac resources.
d. Insurance Acceptance Status, identifying whether each facility accepts U.S. Government employee medical
insurance plans and any known payment requirements, pre‑payment expectations, or dispute‑resolution
considerations.
e. Facility Use Recommendations, including NASA‑specific considerations and any operational limitations or
risk factors.
f. Regional Risk Assessment, summarizing relevant geopolitical, infrastructure, transportation, or environmental
risks, along with proposed mitigation strategies.
g. Transport and Access Considerations, including typical timelines and constraints for access to airports, border
crossings, restricted areas, or local authorities.
h. Verification and Validation Procedures, describing how the Contractor annually confirms the accuracy of
facility information, capabilities, and points of contact data.
rows.normalized: Continuation of Medical Facility Support Plan required contents, items c-h (8 items total across pages 7-8).

rows.verbatim:
2.3.4. The Contractor shall establish and provide, within 60 calendar days of contract start and maintain for the duration
of the contract, the GOP advance service agreements with the specific medical facilities that NASA identifies as
critical medical facilities in Russia and Kazakhstan.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall establish, provide (within 60 days) and maintain GOP advance service agreements with NASA-identified critical medical facilities in Russia and Kazakhstan.

rows.verbatim:
If the Contractor cannot establish a GOP advance service
agreement at one of NASA’s identified medical facilities in Russia/Kazakhstan by the end of that 60-day period,
then the Contractor shall notify the NASA COR and provide an alternate course of action to meet the intent of the
GOP advance service agreement.
rows.normalized: If Contractor cannot establish a GOP advance service agreement within 60 days, it shall notify the COR and provide an alternate course of action.

rows.verbatim:
Annually by December 15th, the Contractor shall provide a written summary
report on the status of GOP advance service agreements for the NASA identified hospitals.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide an annual written status report on GOP advance service agreements by December 15th.

rows.verbatim:
2.3.5. The Contractor shall establish and provide, within 60 calendar days of contract start and updated annually for
currency by Oct 1st, a written medevac plan of action/response for each location that NASA frequently visits to
include Moscow, Russia; Baikonur, Kazakhstan; Karaganda, Kazakhstan; Nordwijk, Netherlands; Montreal,
Canada; Tsukuba, Japan; and Tanegashima, Japan.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall establish and provide (within 60 days, updated annually) a medevac plan of action for listed frequent-visit locations.
The medevac plan shall include at a minimum items a-h (8 items) covering POCs, country requirements, facilities, access, risk assessment, insurance, data needs, and verification procedures.

rows.verbatim:
2.3.6. The Contractor shall provide, within 10 calendar days of contract start, a secure electronic registration capability
that:
a. Provides travelers with a description of the scope of Contractor’s services in accordance with this SOW.
b. Educates travelers on specific instructions to follow should a medical incident or emergency occur and
traveler’s responsibilities in accordance with this SOW.
c. Captures critical information from travelers that expedites medical assistance and evacuation when
necessary.
d. Meets industry standards for data protection, accessibility, storage, and retention requirements of private
medical and personal information (e.g. Personally Identifiable Information, Health Insurance, etc.).
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide, within 10 days of contract start, a secure electronic registration capability meeting requirements a-d (4 items).

rows.verbatim:
2.3.7. The Contractor shall provide a weekly report on current and historical NASA traveler enrollment and critical
traveler information.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide a weekly report on traveler enrollment and critical traveler information.

rows.verbatim:
2.3.9. The Contractor shall provide, by Sept 30th annually, a summary report of all medical incidents by date and
incidence level (Levels 1-4), medical evacuations, reservations and call-ups of medical transport via air
ambulance for Soyuz landings (if executed) supported by the Contractor during that year.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide an annual summary report (by Sept 30) of medical incidents, evacuations, and Soyuz landing support activities.

Reservation Readiness Package consisting of a dedicated tail-number assignment, overflight and landing permits,
diplomatic route clearances, aircraft medical and transport capabilities, and staffing plan.

notification to the Contractor no later than 36 hours prior to the Soyuz landing event.

associated NASA flight surgeon shall be transported to Houston, Texas.

Contractor shall activate the asset and personnel and provide an Operational Deployment Package consisting of a
copy of the officially filed International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) flight plan, crew-rest compliance,
real-time satellite tracking link, confirmation of NASA passengers on flight manifest, finalized staffing plan, and
communications matrix.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall activate asset/personnel and provide an Operational Deployment Package (ICAO flight plan, crew-rest compliance, tracking link, manifest confirmation, staffing plan, comms matrix) within 3 hours of NASA call-up.

transport via air ambulance shall be the responsibility of the Contractor and no additional cost beyond the prepaid
reservation fee and call-up fee as specified in Section B Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Group Membership amount will
